text.p: Polish Bank Handlowy brokerage advised investors to hold shares of the Okocim brewer, saying it had good development prospects thanks to its strategic shareholder -- Denmark's Carlsberg .
It said in its report dated November 15, that Carlsberg spoke for the firm's growth but strong competition among Polish brewers and Okocim's poor advertising could slow the dynamic of the profits.
Handlowy said forecasted growth of beer consumption in Poland and Okocim's large variety of high quality products could contribute to the firm's good performance.
It said, however, the elimination of customs duties in 1998 on imports from CEFTA countries and in 1999 from EU was likely to negatively influence all beer producers in Poland, including Okocim.
It said it expected Okocim's net profit to rise to 27 million zlotys in 1996 and to 38 million in 1997, up from last year's 14.1 million.
It saw its sales rising to 203 million this year and to 244 million next year, up from 156 million in 1995.
Okocim closed at 16 zlotys on Monday. On November 15 it traded at 17 zlotys.
